claims.claim_text: Indexed Anthony Visini is probably the corporal named in a 1944 OSS personnel survey in Italy.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The direct OSS report names Cpl. Anthony Visini, records an Army-entry date matching the adjacent Antonio Visini Army record, and describes OSS training and installation duties.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable from the exact rare name and direct OSS context, but the index row has no printed identifier and may duplicate the separately preserved Antonio row.
claims.temporal_assessment: The report documents OSS-period duties, not a pre-OSS employer; the personnel file is required to resolve the two index rows.
claims.match_notes: No wartime OSS duty is converted into a pre-OSS employer. The Anthony and Antonio rows remain separate and visibly grouped for duplicate review.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Colonel Valentine P.T. Viviani is probably the British officer Valentine Patrick Terrel Vivian.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare given name and initials, colonel-level rank and British Army note align with official Gazette notices for Valentine Patrick Terrel Vivian.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high confidence because the surname differs by a final i and neither Gazette notice names OSS or Box 806.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1939 notice establishes a prewar British military commission; the exact relation to the OSS-index file remains unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The original Viviani spelling is preserved. No Secret Intelligence Service role is inferred from these notices.

claims.claim_text: The probable Valentine Patrick Terrel Vivian match held a British Army commission effective 3 September 1939 and later appeared as a temporary lieutenant-colonel on the General List.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1940 Gazette identifies him as a major, late Indian Army Reserve of Officers, commissioned without pay and allowances; the 1947 Gazette lists him as a temporary lieutenant-colonel, General List.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity from the rare full name reconstructed from initials, rank and British Army note.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1939 commission is definitely pre-OSS; continuity and immediate predecessor status are not established.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment, not civilian employment; excluded from verified-employer analytics.
